subject: Private endpoint exit IP ownership, firewall responsibilities, and next steps
content:
From: Alicia Romero <alicia.romero@bluecrest.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:14:23 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: exit IPs and firewall ownership (initial request)

Hi Tessa / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. We are preparing a private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoint) for BlueCrest and the security team has two hard asks before procurement can proceed:

- A definitive list of IPs/FQDNs the control plane will originate from for outbound traffic so we can put rules in place (egress to telemetry, upgrade checks, license validation).
- A recommended ownership model for who manages firewall rules and rotation (customer-managed NAT vs Redwood-managed egress IP allocation).

Our environment is strict: no wildcard outbound, TLS inspection is on, and any third-party endpoints must be allowlisted by IP. The deadline for the procurement package is next Friday — can you provide a mapping and a short operational model we can hand to our network team?

Attached: initial network sketch (internal).

Thanks,
Alicia Romero
Director, Cloud Ops — BlueCrest Logistics
[Attachment: sketch-network.png (image)]

---

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Romero <alicia.romero@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 13:02:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: exit IPs and firewall ownership (initial request)

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and the sketch.

High level answers up front:
1) We can provide a short list of stable egress IPs per region for the Redwood control plane (recommended for allowlisting for telemetry, telemetry ingestion, license checks).
2) For customer-facing model traffic coming from your private endpoint, we support two modes:
   - Customer-managed NAT: You own the egress IPs and rotate on your cadence.
   - Redwood-assigned static exit IPs (recommended if you want minimal config on your side).

Pros/cons (short):
- Customer NAT: full control, aligns with strict outbound policies; more ops work for you.
- Redwood-assigned: less operational burden but requires trust in our documented rotation windows and RFC-style change notifications.

I put together a quick CSV mapping to start (exit-ip-map.csv) showing the control plane IPs we can publish, recommended firewall rules (ip + port + proto), and suggested ownership tags. See the attached.

Next steps I propose:
- Jonas: can you add technical notes about proxying and TLS inspection implications?
- Michael: please confirm the expected DNS/FQDNs the control plane will use (we prefer FQDNs plus IPs when possible).
- Alicia: if you prefer the Redwood static-exit model, we'll send a contract appendix and an operational SLA for IP change windows.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Manager, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: exit-ip-map.csv (csv)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Romero <alicia.romero@bluecrest.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 10:47:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: exit IPs and firewall ownership (initial request)

Adding technical context below (networking team perspective):

1) NAT vs Redwood-managed exit IPs (details)
- Customer NAT (preferred for highest isolation): BlueCrest keeps control of its NAT gateway(s). All outbound traffic from private endpoints egress through your owned IPs. Redwood will rely on the peer/provider path — we will publish required destination FQDNs and ports but *not* the source IPs.
- Redwood static exit IPs (operational model): Redwood will allocate a small, stable pool of egress IPs per region (we suggest /29 per customer to start). We commit to a 30-day advance notification for any permanent change and a 72-hour notice for emergency rotations.

2) TLS inspection and SNI-based allowlisting
- If your security stack requires SNI/DNS-level allowlisting (preferred vs IP-only because we may use ephemeral service IPs behind CDNs), provide us the allowed FQDNs. Where TLS inspection breaks certificate pinning or mTLS, customer NAT is the safer option.

3) Control plane vs data plane separation
- Our recommendation: allowlist control plane IPs (for telemetry, updates) separately from data-plane model-serving endpoints. Data-plane model requests should be routed to the private endpoint inside the VPC (no egress). Any outbound callbacks (webhooks, analytics pings) must be explicitly enumerated.

4) Minimal firewall rule set (example)
- 52.142.34.10/32 tcp:443 -> redwood-controlplane-us1.redwood.ai (TLS)
- 52.142.34.11/32 tcp:443 -> telemetry-ingest.redwood.ai
- 52.142.34.12/32 tcp:8443 -> licensing.redwood.ai (mutual TLS)

5) Operational recommendations
- Use short, documented maintenance windows for IP rotations.
- Implement synthetic test pings to the listed FQDNs and alert on failures.
- Keep a signed notarized attestation (policy doc) that maps who within BlueCrest can request firewall changes.

I attached a short PDF that outlines how to map CIDR blocks to roles and a sample ACL.

Jonas Weber
Principal Network Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: controlplane-egress-guidance.pdf (pdf)]

Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 08:30:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: exit IPs and firewall ownership (initial request)

Alicia — summarizing and proposed assignment so we can get this into procurement: 

Decisions & ask:
1) BlueCrest to confirm preferred ownership model by EOD Monday: "customer-managed NAT" or "Redwood-assigned static exit IPs".
2) If you choose Redwood-assigned: we will supply the final /29 and SLA addendum; BlueCrest security must accept the 72-hour emergency rotation window.
3) Network team should allowlist the three control-plane CIDRs in the attached CSV for now and prefer FQDN-based rules where possible.

Action owners:
- BlueCrest (Alicia / Samir): decide ownership model and share the internal firewall approvers list.
- Redwood (Jonas): finalize the exact IPs and provide a conformance test plan (synthetic checks + sample curl responses).
- Redwood (Michael): confirm DNS names + add them to the HubSpot deal notes.

I'll create a Confluence page with the final mapping and copy the permission matrix so your auditors have a single artifact to reference. Once BlueCrest confirms, we'll produce a short SOC/attestation bundle for procurement.

Please reply to confirm next steps or flag anything missing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
